longName: Fulfill the EDFacts FS002 Special Education Federal Reporting Requirement
scope: One SEA's annual FS002 submission to EDFacts, end to end: assembly and validation in the state system through acceptance by EDPass.
frequency: Annually, on the federal EDFacts submission cycle.

keyConcepts.definition: A U.S. Department of Education initiative that centralizes K-12 performance data supplied by state education agencies with other departmental data assets, to support policy, management, and budget decisions.
The EDFacts file specification for IDEA Part B child count and educational environments — 19 data elements, reported as aggregate counts derived from per-student source data.
The modernized, centralized data submission application the Department uses to collect, validate, and process elementary and secondary education data from SEAs.

openIssues: DATA TABLE TO REVISIT. Issue #5's Data table cites Credential Award (CEDS C200079), Credential Definition (C200087), Competency Definition (C200065), and the IMS OpenBadge v3p0 JSON schema — the same rows that appear in the LER issuance issues, which look to have carried over while the issue template was being worked out. An IDEA Part B child count wants a different set. The case is grounded here on the FS002 elements carried by the already-authored FS002 family, and the original rows are noted so the authors can swap them in at leisure. Worth noting for the standard's own sake: rendering them as given would still have satisfied the data-grounding invariant, since they are real CEDS classes with real identifiers. A conformance check cannot tell a correct citation from a relevant one — a useful thing to learn early.

OVERLAP WITH AN EXISTING CASE. This case covers the same ground as uc:fs002-package-submission, authored in the v0.8 worked example at summary level with the same primary actor, trigger, and scope. That the two were written independently is exactly what one expects while a corpus is being seeded. It is rendered here as its own node and related by `duplicate` so an editor can decide whether to merge them — which, under the standard's editor-adjudication rule, is a human decision by design rather than something the loader should guess.

Issue #5's two steps sit at different altitudes. Step 1 ('assemble and validate the 19 data elements, generate the aggregate counts, enable quality control and analysis') is an entire user-goal case — uc:fs002-compilation — held in one line. Step 2 is EDPass's side of the submission. At summary level that compression is perfectly legitimate; it is simply why this case reads as brief beside its siblings.

Brandon assigned the field completion to Greg Nadeau in the issue comments, so the issue is vetted for relevance with its detail still to come. Several slots below are PROPOSED from the EDFacts documentation and the existing FS002 family rather than supplied by the issue, and are offered as a starting point for that work.

The FS002 family's own long-standing open item applies here: the stated methodology and the applied methodology must agree (cond:stated-equals-applied-methodology), which no step in this summary rendering enforces.

actors.role: The designated SEA official who acts as primary liaison with the U.S. Department of Education for submission of annual K-12 performance, demographic, and program data.
actors.interest: The state meets its federal reporting obligation accurately and on time.

actors.role: Receives, validates, and processes the submitted FS002 data.
actors.interest: Submitted data conforms to the published FS002 specification.

actors.actor: SEA IDEA Part B Data Manager
actors.role: Produces the child count and educational environments data file from state source data.
actors.interest: Counts are unduplicated, reproducible, and defensible.

interestedParties.interest: The state's IDEA Section 618 reporting is complete and timely.
Reported environments reflect actual state placement practice.

condition.statement: The SEA's FS002 submission is accepted by EDPass, and the state has met the federal IDEA Part B child count and educational environments reporting requirement.
No FS002 package is transmitted that the state cannot reproduce from its source data and stated methodology; a failed submission leaves the state's record of what was reported unchanged.
